title: In vivo quantification of mitochondria-associated ER membranes in C. elegans
author: Borbolis, Palikaras
materials: Timing: Variable (dependent on image number and quality)

steps.title: Prepare NGM plates
steps.instruction: Make Nematode Growth Medium (NGM), autoclave, cool, add supplements, pour into 60 mm plates and let solidify.

substeps.instruction: Pour 700 mL distilled water (dH₂O) into a 1 L glass bottle or conical flask and add a magnetic stirring bar.
Add while stirring: 3 g NaCl, 2 g Bacto peptone, 0.2 g Streptomycin, and 17 g agar (agar will dissolve only after sterilization).
Fill a second container with ~400 mL dH₂O.
Cover both containers and autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min (use separate dH₂O bottle to avoid overflow).
Cool the medium to 55–60 °C (water bath or air) until it can be touched comfortably for several seconds.
Add under aseptic conditions: 1 mL CaCl₂ (1 M), 1 mL MgSO₄ (1 M), 25 mL KPO₄ pH 6 (1 M), 1 mL Cholesterol (5 mg/mL), 1 mL Nystatin (10 mg/mL), then bring volume to 1 L with sterile dH₂O.
Alternative: prepare directly in a 2 L bottle with 975 mL dH₂O and add the same reagents.
Pour 8 mL of the medium into each 60 mm petri dish using a peristaltic pump.
Allow plates to solidify for at least 12 h.
Store plates upside‑down at 4 °C for up to one month (avoid longer storage to prevent salt concentration changes).

steps.title: Seed NGM plates with OP50
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli OP50 and spread it onto the prepared NGM plates.

substeps.instruction: Streak a small amount of frozen OP50 (from –80 °C glycerol stab) onto a 90 mm LB plate containing Streptomycin 200 µg/mL and incubate at 37 °C for ~12 h.
Pick a single colony and inoculate 50 mL liquid LB in a conical flask.
Grow at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm for ~6 h until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.9–1.2 (alternative: 22–25 °C for ~16 h to reach the same OD).
Apply 200 µL of the OP50 culture to the centre of each NGM plate, then gently swirl in a cyclic motion to spread the bacteria, avoiding the plate edges.
Incubate plates for ~16 h at 22–25 °C to allow a bacterial lawn to develop.
Store seeded plates upside‑down at 4 °C; use freshly seeded plates for experiments.

steps.title: Supplement NGM plates (optional)
steps.instruction: Irradiate plates and apply chemical compounds while keeping solvent concentrations low.

substeps.instruction: Irradiate seeded plates with 25 J/cm² UVC using a UV crosslinker, lids off; keep plates protected from light after irradiation.
Prepare a working solution of each compound so that 100–200 µL will be spotted on each plate to reach the desired final concentration.
Spot the appropriate volume onto the plate surface, let diffuse for 1–2 h before use.
For compounds dissolved in DMSO or ethanol, keep final solvent concentration below 1 % (DMSO) or 0.5 % (ethanol).
Alternative: add compounds directly to the NGM medium in step 1f or to the OP50 liquid culture before seeding if bacterial metabolism is not a concern.

steps.title: Create reusable ROI pattern
steps.instruction: Generate and save a 125 × 125 pixel selection that will be reused for sub‑image extraction.

substeps.instruction: Launch Fiji.
File → New (Ctrl+N); set image type to 8‑bit, size 125 × 125 pixels, OK.
Select All (Ctrl+A).
Press T to add the selection to the ROI Manager, then More → Save in the ROI Manager.

steps.title: Import acquired image
steps.instruction: Open a confocal image with Bio‑Formats and keep it as a composite hyperstack.

substeps.instruction: Drag‑and‑drop or File → Open the image.
In the Bio‑Formats Import Options, set Color Mode to Composite, leave all other boxes unchecked, and click OK.

steps.title: Select ROIs and duplicate sub‑images
steps.instruction: Choose well‑focused regions, duplicate them as hyperstacks, and save with traceable names.

substeps.instruction: Identify a well‑focused region with clear signal in both channels.
In the ROI Manager, select the saved 125 × 125 pixel pattern.
Transfer the ROI onto the chosen region and duplicate via Image → Duplicate (Ctrl+Shift+D); ensure “Duplicate hyperstack” is checked.
Save the duplicated sub‑image (File → Save or S) using a consistent name that links it to the original image and experimental condition.
Repeat for a second region (or more for heterogeneous images).

steps.title: Subtract background
steps.instruction: Reduce image noise by background subtraction with a fixed rolling‑ball radius.

substeps.instruction: Process → Subtract Background.
Set Rolling Ball Radius to 50.0 pixels; leave all other options unchecked.
Make sure the “Light background” box is unchecked, then OK.

steps.title: Create RGB duplicate
steps.instruction: Generate a colored version of the background‑subtracted image for visual inspection.

substeps.instruction: Image → Type → RGB Color (this creates the colocalization image).

steps.title: Split channels
steps.instruction: Separate the two fluorescence channels into individual grayscale images.

substeps.instruction: Select the original (background‑subtracted) image.
Image → Color → Split Channels.

steps.title: Create binary masks for each channel
steps.instruction: Convert each channel to a binary mask and apply a median filter (radius 0.5 px).

substeps.instruction: For the mOrange channel:
Process → Binary → Convert to Mask.
Process → Binary → Median; set radius to 0.5 pixels.
For the GFP channel:
Repeat the Convert to Mask and Median steps.

steps.title: Outline mitochondria
steps.instruction: Generate an outline image of the mitochondrial (GFP) mask.

substeps.instruction: Select the binary GFP image.
Process → Binary → Outline.

steps.title: Calculate MAMs colocalization
steps.instruction: Identify the overlapping area between mitochondrial outlines and ER (mOrange) mask.

substeps.instruction: Process → Image Calculator.
Set Image 1 = mOrange binary, Image 2 = GFP binary.
Choose operation AND, check “Create new window”, then OK.

steps.title: Create selection from MAMs image
steps.instruction: Convert the colocalization result into a ROI for measurement.

substeps.instruction: Edit → Selection → Create Selection (on the MAMs image).

steps.title: Validate MAMs selection
steps.instruction: Confirm that the selection correctly marks regions where GFP overlaps mOrange.

substeps.instruction: Select the RGB colocalization image (step 8).
Edit → Selection → Restore Selection (or Shift+E).
Visually verify that the grey areas (overlap) are selected; if not, adjust rolling‑ball radius, median filter radius, or thresholding and repeat steps 7–12.

steps.title: Measure mitochondrial surface area
steps.instruction: Quantify the total mitochondrial membrane area in the sub‑image.

substeps.instruction: Analyze → Set Measurements; check Area and Display Label only.
Select the mitochondria outline image.
Edit → Selection → Create Selection.
Analyze → Measure (or press M).

steps.title: Measure MAMs area
steps.instruction: Quantify the area of mitochondrial membrane that colocalizes with ER.

substeps.instruction: Select the MAMs (AND) image.
Edit → Selection → Create Selection.
Analyze → Measure (or press M).

steps.title: Calculate MAMs fraction
steps.instruction: Compute the percentage of mitochondrial surface involved in MAMs and average across sub‑images.

substeps.instruction: Apply the formula: (MAMs area ÷ Mitochondrial surface area) × 100.
Average the resulting percentages for all sub‑images derived from the same original image (one animal).

steps.title: Run batch analysis macro
steps.instruction: Automate steps 7–14 for many sub‑images using an ImageJ macro.

substeps.instruction: Launch Fiji and go to Plugins → New → Macro.
Paste the provided macro code (includes parameters: Rolling Ball Radius = 50, Median Filter Radius Channel 1 = 0.5, Channel 2 = 0.5).
Save the macro (File → Save).
Run the macro: click Run, then in the first dialog set the input folder (sub‑images) and output folder; set file suffix (e.g., .tif).
In the second dialog enter the analysis parameters determined during single‑image validation (Rolling Ball Radius, Median Filter Radii).
The macro will process each sub‑image, generate three .tif files (mitochondrial surface, MAMs overlay, overlay on surface) and a Results.txt file with quantified areas.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Import the Results.txt data, compute MAMs percentages, and perform appropriate statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Open Results.txt in spreadsheet software.
Calculate MAMs percentage for each sub‑image using the same formula as step 18.
Average percentages per animal (all sub‑images from one original image).
For each condition and time point, plot the average MAMs fraction per animal (grouped bar or box plot) and assess significance with two‑way ANOVA (display individual animal points, SD error bars).
Optionally, plot mean MAMs fraction across time points, compute area under the curve (AUC) for each condition, and compare AUC values with t‑tests or one‑way ANOVA.
